standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.

standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.

standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.

standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.

standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.

standing_gaps: No public verified list of emergency obstetric facilities with coordinates exists for Chennai. The facility list is a hand-checked proxy.
No 108 ambulance data is public. Ambulance starts and times are simulated.
No open flood extent exists for the 1-4 Dec 2015 peak. The observed scenario is a composite of available layers.
Roads are current OpenStreetMap roads, not 2015 roads.
additional: Facilities are a hand-checked proxy list of 5 GCC emergency obstetric units; only those on the road graph are routed on, and none is phone-verified.
Mild, moderate and severe are seeded nested subsets (10%, 20%, 35%) of street-level flood reports. They are arbitrary sensitivity settings, not physical flood models and not predictions.
The observed layer is a composite of OpenCity layers with no dates; it is not the 1-4 December 2015 peak and is not routed on.
Edge thresholds (10% and 50% of length flooded), the 3x at-risk time multiplier and the 30-minute coverage threshold are assumptions, not standards.
Travel times use free-flow speeds from OpenStreetMap, so they are comparative, not real response times.
Sample origins are seeded graph nodes in the largest connected road component; all are near flooded areas.
Tamil and Hindi interface text are draft translations until reviewed by fluent speakers.

Population is Census 2011 by ward (2008 ward boundaries), assumed evenly spread inside each ward and scaled to the part of the ward inside the study zone; it is old and approximate. Coverage weights each of the 20 sample origins by its ward's population.
